The company demonstrates superior operational efficiency, delivering a return on assets of 6.55% versus the sector benchmark of 6.18%, a return on equity of 12.36% against 9.21%, and a return on capital employed of 12.74% compared to 9.59% [E8, E9, E10]. Long-term performance highlights robust compounding, led by a 10-year compounded profit growth rate of 38% and a median return on equity of 21% over the same decade [E18, E26]. Recent growth momentum is strong, evidenced by a 28% compounded sales growth rate over the trailing twelve months and quarterly sales expansion of 21% year-on-year [E17, E67]. Institutional interest has grown significantly over the medium term, with foreign institutions increasing their holding to 7.28% and domestic institutions rising to 2.91% from near zero bases in September 2023 [E42, E43]. GRM Overseas Ltd is currently trading at a compelling discount relative to its sector peers, offering a P/E ratio of 24.57x against a sector benchmark of 30.8x and a P/B ratio of 3.05x compared to the sector's 3.82x [E6, E7]. The company displays superior capital efficiency, generating an ROA of 6.55%, an ROE of 12.36%, and an ROCE of 12.74%, all of which outperform their respective sector benchmarks of 6.18%, 9.21%, and 9.59% [E8, E9, E10]. Long-term wealth creation remains intact through a 10-year compounded profit growth of 38% and a median 10-year return on equity of 21% [E18, E26]. Recent operational momentum is accelerating, highlighted by a 28% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months alongside strong near-term catalysts such as expected good quarters and profits up quarter-on-quarter [E17, E59, E69]. Furthermore, institutional sponsorship reveals emerging smart-money accumulation, with foreign institutional holdings increasing to 7.28% and domestic institutional holdings rising to 2.91% from near-zero levels since September 2023 [E42, E43]. Conceded: the stock trades near its 52-week lows with negative trailing price performance and weak recent cash flows [E5, E35, E48, E52].

Conceded: the data provider key-ratios list a P/E of 24.57x and P/B of 3.05x [E6, E7]. However, filed statements confirm the actual traded valuation sits at a far more expensive P/E of 34.4 and a P/B of 3.32x, exposing a serious valuation disconnect [E1, E2]. While the bull highlights superior capital efficiency, the company's return on equity has compressed to 11.3% and ROCE to 11.3%, pulling down recent metrics [E12, E13]. Conceded: 10-year compounded profit growth is robust at 38% and median 10-year ROE reached 21% [E18, E26]. Nonetheless, momentum has completely stalled, evidenced by 3-year compounded profit growth of 0% and trailing 12-month profit growth of just 4% [E20, E21]. Furthermore, the claim of smart-money accumulation ignores recent negative money flow with an institutional holding change of -2.22 percentage points and an overall promoter reduction of 8.66 percentage points [E41, E44]. Finally, the cited trailing sales growth of 28% masks severe underlying deterioration, including negative 3-year sales growth of -3%, a cash conversion of -1.15x, and negative operating cash flow of Rs -61 Cr [E16, E17, E34, E35].
